# From building solar assets to operating them smarter


#


### What AI means for Japan’s renewable energy market and what operators should weigh before bringing it into their workflows.


**Japan’s solar market is entering a different phase.**


For years, the focus was largely on building renewable energy assets and securing the conditions needed to make those projects work. But as **the market moves beyond the FIT era** ,


that is no longer enough. Power price uncertainty, output curtailment, rising costs and the growing role of BESS are changing what it takes to operate a profitable renewable energy asset.


**Want to hear the actual discussion?**


#


[Watch the webinar replay](https://youtu.be/ggnuSm-qUBc)


The question is becoming less about how to build more assets, and more about how to get more from the assets already in operation.


That was the focus of our recent webinar, hosted by **Mike Benner** of **PMC Ltd.** , with **Yuko Ishihara** of **Photon Capital** and **Govinda Upadhyay** of **SmartHelio** , where we discussed what AI can actually do for Japan’s solar and BESS market


## Japan's solar market is entering a new operating phase


During the FIT era, the fundamentals of developing a solar project were relatively straightforward. Secure the land, obtain the necessary permits and approvals, and secure grid capacity.


Today, there are many more variables to manage. **Curtailment, electricity prices, battery integration, trading and day-to-day plant performance all matter more than they used to** . At the same time, higher insurance, financing and operating costs are putting pressure on project returns.


> The operation side becomes more important than before.
> **Yuko Ishihara, Photon Capital**


That changes the role of the asset owner and operator. It is no longer enough to build a plant and keep it running. Operators need to understand what is happening across the portfolio and find problems before they start affecting performance.


And that is where operational data becomes much more valuable.

## Where AI can make a practical difference


The discussion looked at AI across several parts of the asset lifecycle, including project screening, due diligence, asset management and trading.


At the development stage, AI can bring together information such as GIS data, land conditions, grid information and permitting requirements to make initial project screening much faster.


But Japan has a particular challenge here. **Important information is not always available in one digital source, and local rules or site conditions can require additional checks.** AI can speed up the first step. It cannot replace local knowledge or verification.


The same applies to due diligence. AI is useful for reviewing contracts, financial models and large volumes of documentation. But technical conditions, permits and site-specific issues often need someone who understands the project and the local context.


This balance between automation and human judgement was an important part of the discussion. AI can take a lot of manual work out of the process. **People still need to be involved where context matters.**


## From detecting faults to acting earlier


**Asset management is where the value of AI becomes particularly clear.**


A traditional monitoring system can tell an operator what happened. The more useful question is what is starting to go wrong, how much it matters and what should be looked at first.


During the webinar, Ishihara shared an example where **SmartHelio identified unusual behaviour across a large number of PCS units. The issue was investigated further and eventually aligned with a manufacturer-identified problem involving sealing and water ingress.**


What mattered was not simply that an anomaly was detected. The pattern was spotted early enough to investigate before the problem became a larger operational issue.


> AI can support the decision, but the final judgement still needs to come from people.
> **Yuko Ishihara, Photon Capital**


That is a meaningful change for asset management. **Instead of waiting for equipment to fail and then trying to understand what happened, operators can look for early signs and decide where action is needed.**


## Why BESS changes the picture


**BESS adds another layer to this operating model.**


A solar plant with a battery is not only producing electricity. The battery can also respond to market conditions, manage energy flows and potentially create additional value through electricity trading.


That opens up **several areas where AI could help,** including generation forecasting, price forecasting, battery optimisation and curtailment management.


But this is still developing in Japan. As Yuko Ishihara explained


, introducing new trading strategies into existing projects can be complicated by project finance structures and the interests of different stakeholders.


The opportunity is there. It needs to be approached with **a clear understanding of the Japanese** market and how individual projects are structured.


## Data, security and the importance of Japan-specific context


One thing became clear throughout the discussion: **AI is only useful when the data behind it is useful.** Some Japanese solar assets do not collect operational data frequently enough for more advanced analysis. In other cases, the data is available but does not carry enough context to explain what is actually happening at the plant.


A simple example from the discussion showed why this matters. **Two PCS units could appear to be performing differently, but a closer look revealed that they had different numbers of connected strings. Without that context, the analysis could easily point in the wrong direction.** This is where human judgement still matters.


There is another question that becomes more important as AI enters renewable energy operations: how is that operational data being handled and protected? Solar and BESS assets are part of critical energy infrastructure, and their operational data can reveal detailed information about plant performance and behaviour. Data security and governance need to be considered alongside AI capabilities, not added later.


> Data security is not something you add at the end.
> **Govinda Upadhyay, SmartHelio**


[Explore GAIA](https://smarthelio.com/gaia/)


The architecture of the AI system matters too. For Japan’s solar and BESS operators, the question is not simply **whether an AI system can analyse plant data.** It is also whether that data can be handled in a secure environment, and whether the resulting insights can be traced back to reliable operational information.


**SmartHelio’s GAIA** **is built specifically for solar and BESS operations, using a secure closed-cloud environment and verified operational data to support traceable insights.**


The wider point is that AI for Japan cannot be a generic solution adapted after the fact. It needs to work with the realities of Japanese projects: local regulations, site conditions, operating practices and data availability.


## What this means for the next phase of solar operations in Japan


The Japanese renewable energy market is moving from a period focused heavily on building assets to one where the **quality of operations will have a much bigger impact on value.** AI can help operators identify problems earlier, prioritise maintenance, understand plant performance and, over time, optimise how solar and BESS assets respond to changing market conditions.


But technology alone will not solve the problem. The data needs to be reliable. The system needs to understand the Japanese operating environment. Operational information needs to be handled securely. And experienced people still need to check the results and make the final call.


> AI is a tool. It’s not the final decision maker.
> **Yuko Ishihara, Photon Capital**


The opportunity is not to replace the people managing Japan’s renewable energy assets. **It is to give them better information, earlier warnings and faster ways to act.** That could be what makes the next generation of Japanese solar and BESS assets not just bigger, but smarter, more secure and more profitable.
